input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Renewals meet the preferred position in full: renewal terms are 12 months (not multi-year), Customer may opt out on only 30 days' written notice, Vendor must send a renewal reminder 60 days beforehand (with the opt-out deadline extended if it fails to do so), and § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. The three-year duration in § 8.1 is the initial term of the master agreement, not an automatic multi-year renewal, so the walk-away trigger is not engaged. No conflicting escalation language appears in § 7. No redline needed.
